To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) it is possible to dynamically allocate computation-specific circuitry to different resources of a modern FPGA, and to execute them concurrently, in order to achieve higher performance and better reliability; (2) the proposed algorithms for runtime allocation of computations onto the FPGA are capable of achieving a higher performance than the static approach of partitioning the circuitry in a fixed way, and they can also be used for improving the reliability of the computations by exploiting the partial reconfiguration capabilities of the FPGA; and

we have developed a novel way to dynamically allocate and schedule computation-specific circuitry onto a partially reconfigurable FPGA in order to maximize the reliability of the system, while at the same time achieving an optimal utilization of its resources and an optimal execution time for the computation tasks.

we have developed a novel approach to dynamically schedule, allocate, and execute real-time computations onto Xilinx FGPAs subject to fault occurrence, that this approach is able to improve the performance and reliability of such FGPAs, and that it has been implemented on real hardware, as shown in the proof-of-concept.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel way to use the computational power of modern FPGAs to achieve a higher performance and a higher reliability, even in the case that the chip has been affected by permanent damage.

the development and implementation of novel techniques that enable FPGAs to dynamically reconfigure and reassign the resources on the chip in order to improve the performance and reliability of the computations that are carried on.

the design and implementation of a novel runtime reconfigurable system that is capable of exploiting the computational capabilities of the FPGA, while being able to cope with the occurrence of faults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the algorithms presented in this paper can be considered as an important step towards a more effective and efficient use of modern FPGA technology.

the algorithms described in this paper provide a novel and effective way to exploit the computational capabilities of modern FPGAs, while at the same time providing a high level of reliability in the presence of faults.
the proposed approach is a promising solution towards the development of reliable, fault-tolerant, and highly performant real-time systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new approach that is able to exploit the computation power of FPGAs in order to improve the reliability of real-time systems.
we have developed a novel approach for the runtime scheduling, allocation, and execution of real-time hardware tasks onto Xilinx FGPAs subject to faults occurrence.

we propose a new way of exploiting FPGA technology to achieve high-performance and reliable computing, which is a very challenging problem in the current era of high-performance and high-reliability systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the future, the use of modern FPGAs will not only be limited to the implementation of a specific application, but will also allow for the dynamic reconfiguration of the hardware in order to achieve a higher performance and a higher reliability, even under adverse circumstances such as the spontaneous emergence of faults and permanent damage in the chip's silicon substrate.
the proposed algorithms can be used to achieve a higher degree of reliability in the execution of real-time computations, even when faults and failures occur in the underlying hardware.
the proposed algorithms are able to achieve a high degree of fault-tolerance while maintaining the overall performance and reliability of the system at a high level.
